answer: Staggered arrival gating. New identities must submit their first transaction in a slot derived from a shared beacon, and their submission pulse must fall within a narrow window opened at dawn of each epoch; the vault holding pending registrations stays sealed until enough distinct slots are filled. An attacker wanting N coordinated sybils must spread them across N epoch-dawns with correct per-slot timing, paying roughly N epochs of delay plus the cost of idle maintained keys waiting for their assigned window.
